Question: What is the relationship between the decline probability of an expert and whether or not they have a "friend" who has already declined?
Evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 1, page 2) (image attached): Figure 1: Decline probability of an expert conditioned on whether or not the expert has a correlated “friend” who has already declined on two datasets: QA-Expert and Paper-Reviewer, and our online evalu- ation of journal reviewer recommendation.
Words printed in the figure: QA-Expert Paper-Reviewer Online Evaluation 0.4 0.5 0.6 0.7 Decline Probability without with
[E2] (figure, Figure 1, page 2): a zoomed view of Figure 1 (image attached) [image]

claims.text: The decline probability of an expert is conditioned on whether or not the expert has a correlated "friend" who has already declined.

cites.quote: Decline probability of an expert conditioned on whether or not the expert has a correlated “friend” who has already declined

claims.text: Based on the bar charts, the decline probability is higher when the expert has a friend who has already declined ("with") compared to when they do not ("without").

cites.observation: In the bar chart for all three categories (QA-Expert, Paper-Reviewer, and Online Evaluation), the orange bar representing "with" is taller than the blue bar representing "without".
